body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-08-28.** The first version flipped the default `claude` profile to process mode. That trades away the agent view (`claude agents`): it lists background sessions only, so a `--bg` root is the one row an operator sees per track, and a process-mode child is invisible there. Visibility is a requirement, so `claude` and `claude-track` **stay `--bg`**. What is left is the CI/container profile, done right, and it is still worth doing.

## Why

`claude-p` is the profile for hosts with no session daemon — CI, containers, an Actions runner. It is also the one launch shape whose worker receives the environment, exits with a code and prints a typed result; it never had #125/#132/#137/#150. But it is a second-class citizen today: it uses `--worktree` (the CLI's own checkout, which the dispatcher cannot name ahead of time), takes no `--session-id`, and its result JSON is truncated to four fields (#155).

## What

- `claude-p` becomes `mode: "process"`, `workspace: "worktree"` — the dispatcher makes `kb-<n>-<k>` with `ensureWorktree` (explicit `git fetch`, `origin/<default>` start point), no `--worktree` flag — with `--session-id {session}` chosen at claim and saved on the attempt row, `--settings {hook_settings}` (from #144), `--setting-sources project`, `--output-format json`, and the existing tool/budget flags.
- `hkb show` prints the `claude --resume <session>` line from the row the moment a `claude-p` attempt is claimed.
- The `claude` and `claude-track` launches are untouched; their identity lands through #150 (no `KB_*` leak) and #144 (`--settings` hooks, verified to fire inside `--bg` sessions). `docs/harnesses.md` says plainly which profile to pick where: `--bg` where a human watches the agent view, `claude-p` where no daemon exists.
- Measure and record whether the `complete`-builtin and heredoc refusals recur when the cwd is an hkb-made worktree without `--worktree` (so far measured only under `--bg --worktree`).

## Constraints

- The protocol does not change: claim → work → verb, one PR per node. Only the `claude-p` launch shape does.
- A pid-mode child is `detached` and survives a one-shot `hkb dispatch`; a `--loop` still reaps it by pid. #136's grace rule applies to it as a `kill(pid)`.
- Nothing here touches Copilot or Codex; they already run as dispatcher-made-worktree processes.

## Done when

- A `claude-p` attempt has `KB_TASK` visible inside the worker, a session id on the row at claim time, and a cost on the row at exit.
- `claude`/`claude-track` boards behave exactly as today; the agent view still shows one row per track.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green; `npm run smoke` green (profiles are read from the package at runtime).
title: claude-p, the CI profile, done right: hkb-made worktree, session id chosen at claim, hooks on the launch line — claude stays --bg
